correctness.rationale: For the explicit Bessel kernel, the convergent positive Gram representation proves compact strict positivity; the simple Perron mode has nonzero overlap with the explicitly positive SEP source, so its negative resolvent pole is real and nonremovable. The critical Feller semigroup Laplace transform gives exact scaling and a substochastic upper bound. The small-time principal eigenvalue follows from a rank-one term plus an O(t^4) positive remainder. The large-time eigenvalue follows from Hilbert-Schmidt convergence of sampled killing to Dirichlet killing, whose ground-state ODE is x f''= -beta f with beta=j_(1,1)^2/4. Inversion yields the exact radius expansions. The standalone executable passed 89 independent symbolic/numerical consistency assertions; finite sampling is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source delivers an exact current-density tilt resolvent but does not quantify where its power series ceases to converge. The claimed exact radius for every finite time plus its singular short/long-time scalings answers a natural analytic question relevant to interpreting high-order current response. The Bessel-zero coefficient comes from a nontrivial sampled-to-continuous killed branching spectrum, rather than a parameter renaming or arbitrary finite slice. The negative pole pinches the physical omega>-1 boundary, giving a concrete large-time control limit; no generality beyond the stated SEP class is claimed.
